title: Concurrent cache tests do not enforce single-flight execution
reasoning: The sequential cache test asserts that get_or_compute calls the producer only once, but the concurrent waiter tests only assert that both callers receive the same value. A regression where both threads or async tasks execute the expensive compute function concurrently would still satisfy these assertions as long as both return "value". That misses the core single-flight behavior these tests appear intended to protect, which matters for duplicate side effects, unnecessary backend calls, and cache stampede prevention.
recommendation: Track a call counter protected by a lock for the threaded test and a simple counter for the async test, then assert the compute function was invoked exactly once after both waiters complete.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The concurrent tests assert waiter completion and returned values, but they never count how many times the compute callback ran under contention.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend test_cache_get_or_compute_waiters_complete and test_cache_get_or_compute_async_waiters_complete to increment a compute call counter and assert it equals 1 after the two callers finish.
minimumFixScope: Update the two concurrent cache tests in tests/backend/test_cache_layer.py to assert single producer invocation under contention.
